executive_summary: Economic activities are classified into Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors. In India, while Tertiary GDP share grew to over 50%, agricultural labor remained stuck at over 44%, creating disguised unemployment.

storyboard.title: The Three Economic Sectors
storyboard.description: Following cotton from farm harvest (Primary) to fabric weaving (Secondary) to retail shop sale (Tertiary).

storyboard.title: Disguised Unemployment in Farming
storyboard.description: Depicting Laxmi's family of 5 working a 2-hectare plot where 2 members produce zero marginal yield.
storyboard.key_takeaway: Underemployment hides surplus labor in agriculture.

video_embeds.title: Organised vs Unorganised Sectors & MGNREGA
video_embeds.transcript_summary: Contrasts Kanta's formal job benefits with Kamal's informal vulnerability, explaining MGNREGA 2005 legal guarantees.

hotspots.popover_content: Primary extracts natural goods, Secondary manufactures processed items, Tertiary provides transport, banking, and trade services.

key_takeaways: GDP includes final goods only to avoid double counting.
Primary sector retains excess labor with low GDP contribution.
MGNREGA 2005 guarantees 100 days of rural wage employment.
Public sector provides essential infrastructure driven by social welfare.
